facts.fact: São Tomé and Príncipe regulators, including the head of its Institute of Innovation and Knowledge, took part in a UNESCO data governance workshop in Maputo, 8 to 10 December 2025, organised with Mozambique's INTIC and Smart Africa, aligned with the Smart Africa Data Governance Blueprint and the African Union Data Policy Framework.

note: Workshop hosted by AGER with ITU and ARCTEL-CPLP, a Portuguese-speaking regulators' association and not an African body; no fact.

facts.fact: Sao Tome and Principe was among six countries whose policymakers and experts attended the Second Lusophone Africa Data Governance Workshop in Luanda on 15-17 June 2026, co-hosted by Angola's data protection agency, Smart Africa, the World Bank, CETIC.br and UNESCO; attendance only, no agreement signed (the document is dated 28 July 2026, the event June).

AUDA-NEPAD launched its Programme for African Developing Island Economies on 24 July 2026 at an African Union ministerial segment in Abidjan, with Sao Tome and Principe named among the seven island states joining a framework that has digital transformation as one of six pillars.
facts.system: AUDA-NEPAD Programme for African Developing Island Economies

note: Webinar series run by a UN university and Brazilian bodies, not an African body; no fact.

systems.system: CPLP Charter of Rights and Principles in Digital Environments
systems.country_label: Carta CPLP de Direitos e Princípios em Ambientes Digitais

note: Charter signed at Sao Tome on 19 July 2024 by the CPLP (Portuguese-language community, including Brazil, Portugal, Timor-Leste), not an African body; no fact.

facts.fact: Sao Tome and Principe's regulator AGER joined ARTAC, the Central African telecoms regulators' assembly, at its Libreville session closing on 21 October 2026, making eight members, according to GabonReview.

note: Regulators attend an EU-funded peer exchange run by SPIDER Center; no African body's own meeting, agreement or membership stated.
CPLP is a language-based body, so other.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports the country is one of ten countries selected for Smart Africa's IDECT project on digital payments and e-commerce policy.

systems.system: IDECT (Institutional Support to Digital Payments and E-Commerce Policies for Cross-Border Trade)

facts.fact: The ATU ratification status table lists Sao Tome and Principe among the Union's member states, with only the 1977 PATU convention acceded to and no signature of the 1999 Constitution.
